.ansq h1.text: Compare Microsoft and Google's enterprise AI strategies and identify opportunities a mid-sized software company should monitor.

.cards.text:
Short answer

Microsoft sells AI through the products companies already pay for, with Copilot inside Microsoft 365 and Azure OpenAI for custom builds. Google leans on its own Gemini models and Vertex AI, and pushes hardest with teams already on Google Cloud and Workspace.

Where they differ
Microsoft bundles AI into seats companies already license, so adoption follows existing contracts.

.doc h2.text: What a mid-sized software company should watch

.doc p.text: Microsoft sells AI through the products companies already pay for, with Copilot inside Microsoft 365 and Azure OpenAI for custom builds. Google leans on its own Gemini models and Vertex AI, and pushes hardest with teams already on Google Cloud and Workspace.

.doc ul.text:
Microsoft bundles AI into seats companies already license, so adoption follows existing contracts.
Google competes on model quality and price per use, backed by its own chips for training and serving.
Both are adding agents that act inside other apps, which is where new spending is moving.

Marketplace listings on Azure and Google Cloud, which decide how easily buyers can pay for your product.
Price changes for model use, which move the cost of every AI feature you ship.
Agent standards for connecting apps, which decide whether their agents can use your product.
